body:
OBSERVED (2026-08-01, adlc 1.7.0): `adlc ticket create --input <file> --json` (dry-run) emits exactly one JSON document. The same command with `--write` emits the ~12KB result document followed by a SECOND top-level JSON document (JSON.parse fails with 'Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 12007'). The second document is emitted only on the write path — likely the journal/evidence or store-status record printed after the create result.

WHY IT MATTERS: the write SUCCEEDS while the parse fails, so any orchestration piping `--write --json` into JSON.parse concludes the operation failed and may retry — minting a duplicate ticket. The failure mode was hit in practice during P0 authoring: the only safe recovery was noticing the store count changed (133 -> 134) before retrying. `--json` output is a machine contract; it must be exactly one parseable document per invocation (or documented NDJSON, which nothing currently documents).

REPRO: (1) write any valid ticket input JSON to /tmp/t.json (title only is enough); (2) `adlc ticket create --input /tmp/t.json --json | node -e 'JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(0))'` — passes; (3) same with `--write` — parse fails, ticket IS created. Clean up the created ticket afterwards or run in a scratch repo initialized with `adlc init`.

FIX SHAPE (locate precisely by reading the create command's write path in packages/tickets — the bin or lib module that prints the create result, then prints again after journaling): under --json, merge everything the write path reports into the single result document (e.g. a `postWrite` or `journal` field) or suppress the second print. Audit the OTHER store-mutating subcommands (update, complete, archive, store recover) for the same double-print pattern on their --write paths and fix uniformly; the repro recipe above applies to each by substituting the subcommand.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
AC1 — single-document contract: for ticket create with --json, both dry-run and --write emit output where JSON.parse of the FULL stdout succeeds. Verify: new test spawning the real CLI in a temp repo fixture, asserting JSON.parse(stdout) succeeds for both modes and that --write actually persisted (store count +1).
AC2 — uniformity: every store-mutating ticket subcommand honoring --json (create, update, complete, archive at minimum; enumerate by reading the bin's subcommand table) passes the same full-stdout JSON.parse assertion on its --write path. Verify: table-driven test over the subcommand list.
AC3 — no information loss: whatever the second document carried is either present in the merged single document or was redundant (justify in the diff which). Verify: test asserts the merged result contains the after-write store hash (or equivalent field the second doc carried).
AC4 — full suite green: npm test.

PROCESS NOTES: packages/tickets is a gated-artifact producer (trust-root adjacent); expect P5 cross-model review per repo standard. Do not edit any existing ticket's body while testing — use temp-repo fixtures, never this repo's live .adlc store.
title: ticket create --write --json emits two concatenated JSON documents; machine-readable output must be exactly one
